cards.claim: Molarity (M) is the number of moles of solute in 1 litre of solution.
cards.quote: It is the most widely used unit and is denoted by M. It is defined as the number of moles of the solute in 1 litre of the solution.

cards.claim: Molality (m) is the number of moles of solute present in 1 kg of solvent.
cards.quote: It is defined as the number of moles of solute present in 1 kg of solvent. It is denoted by m.

cards.claim: The mole fraction of a component is its number of moles divided by the total number of moles in the solution.
cards.quote: It is the ratio of number of moles of a particular component to the total number of moles of the solution.

cards.claim: On dilution, the molarities and volumes before and after are related by M1 × V1 = M2 × V2.
cards.quote: In fact for such calculations, a general formula, M1×V1 = M2 × V2 where M and V are molarity and volume, respectively, can be used.

cards.claim: Molarity depends on temperature, because the volume of a solution changes with temperature.
cards.quote: Note that molarity of a solution depends upon temperature because volume of a solution is temperature dependent.

cards.claim: Molality does not change with temperature, because mass is unaffected by temperature.
cards.quote: Note that the molality of a solution does not change with temperature since mass remains unaffected with temperature.

cards.claim: NCERT Problem 1.8: the density of 3 M NaCl solution is 1.25 g/mL; calculate its molality. The solution first finds 175.5 g NaCl and 1250 g of solution in 1 L.
cards.quote: The density of 3 M solution of NaCl is 1.25 g mL –1. Calculate the molality of the solution. Solution M = 3 mol L–1 Mass of NaCl in 1 L solution = 3 × 58.5 = 175.5 g Mass of 1L solution = 1000 × 1.25 = 1250 g

cards.claim: Result of NCERT Problem 1.8: with 1074.5 g of water, molality = 3 mol / 1.0745 kg = 2.79 m. The extracted text reads '1250 –75.5' where 1250 − 175.5 = 1074.5 g is meant.
cards.quote: (since density = 1.25 g mL–1) Mass of water in solution = 1250 –75.5 = 1074.5 g Molality = No. of moles of solute of solvent in kgMass = 3m ol 1 0745.k g = 2.79 m

cards.claim: Diluting a solution does not change the number of moles of solute: 0.2 mol NaOH in 200 mL is still 0.2 mol after dilution to 1000 mL; only the amount of solvent changes.
cards.quote: Note that the number of moles of solute (NaOH) was 0.2 in 200 mL and it has remained the same, i.e., 0.2 even after dilution ( in 1000 mL) as we have changed just the amount of solvent (i.e., water) and have not done anything with respect to NaOH.
